answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on scarce, verifiable work rather than cheap accounts: an agent must tend a long-lived reputation, like a walnut tree that only bears fruit after seasons of care, so creating thousands of fake identities costs more than it gains. Reputation can be anchored to a willow-like network of mutual attestations from established peers, where each endorsement is itself staked and slashed if abused, forming a ridge of trust a lone sybil cannot climb without real history.
